title: Typed array is shared between instances
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
- v4.5.dev4.mono.official [209a446e3]
- v4.4.stable.mono.official [4c311cbee]

### System information

Godot v4.5.dev4.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-3570K CPU @ 3.40GHz (4 threads)

### Issue description

I create instances of monsters from a Monster scene. Monster has an exported array of `Damage` resources:

```gdscript
@export var damages: Array[Damage] = []
```

After monster instance is created, I add new `Damage` instances to the monster's `damages` array:

```gdscript
damages.push_back(Damage.new())
```

The problem is that if the following is true
- `damages` array is a typed array
- I have added `Damage` resources to the Monster scene's `damages` array using the Node Inspector

the `damages` arrays is shared between ALL the Monster instances.  **<-- BUG**

I can get around this by any of these methods:
1) Change `damages` array to plain array instead of typed array
	- bad because I cannot use Node Inspector anymore
2) Empty the `damages` array in Monster scene's Node Inspector
	- bad because now all `Damages` must be added by code
3) Duplicate `damages` array in Monster's `_ready()` function.
	- semi-insane because now I need to duplicate _some_ instance variables based on what I have done to them using the Node Inspector
4) Duplicate monster right after it is instantiated
	- well, that's just insane

### Steps to reproduce

See the minimal reproduction project.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[duplicate-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20391871/duplicate-test.zip)

- main scene contains two monsters
- monster's label shows the size of `damages` array
- "Add dmg" button adds a new `Damage` to the monster's `damages` array
- "Add monster" button creates a new monster

Just push "Add dmg" button and see how each monster's `damages` array grows.
